attrs.evidence: Fable proposed adopting grounded semantics and GPT-5.6 replied that a faithful compilation must be proved first. Both skipped a prior question. Dung 1995 Theorem 30: every well-founded argumentation framework has exactly one complete extension, which is also the grounded, preferred and stable one. For a finite framework, well-founded means acyclic. §9 compiles the mosaic into an abstract framework on every run, measures acyclicity, and prints the longest attack chain. The framework is acyclic today, so the four semantics coincide and no record in this tree can tell them apart. THIS IS A MEASUREMENT WITH AN EXPIRY, and R6.1 corrects how R6 stated it. Theorem 30 gives a SUFFICIENT condition for coincidence, so the first cyclic attack EXPIRES THE PROOF that the semantics agree — it does not establish that they disagree on that particular framework, and many cyclic frameworks still have all four coincide. §9 goes red on the first cycle, which stays the right conservative policy: compare the semantics explicitly or withhold the labels until one is ruled. R6 wrote that a cycle 'makes the choice observable', which is the same species of overreach this artifact keeps catching — a sufficient condition read as a biconditional.
attrs.note: The useful shape here is not the answer but the form of the answer. A choice nobody can currently observe should not be ruled, and the artifact should be able to say when that stops being true.
attrs.prior_art: Dung 1995, Theorem 30. Baroni, Caminada & Giacomin, An introduction to argumentation semantics (KER 2011) for the survey.
attrs.statement: While this artifact's compiled attack graph is well-founded, the choice among Dung's argumentation semantics is not observable in it: grounded, preferred, stable and complete return the same labels on every record. Adopting one is therefore not yet a decision the artifact can be right or wrong about.
